suggestions.title: MCP run_builds (and schedule_todo) still start work for a same-team todo whose project belongs to another team, unlike chief run_builds after this PR
suggestions.evidence: The MCP run_builds loop calls only `requireTeamTodo(db, todoId, ctx.teamId)` and then `startBuilds(svc, { projectId: row.projectId, ... })`. It has no requireProjectRow(db, row.projectId, ctx.teamId) check. Chief run_builds (chief-tools.ts:818-821) now runs that check for every task before startBuilds. schedule_todo (mcp-face.ts:394-402) has the same shape and passes row.projectId to createSchedule unchecked.
suggestions.failurePath: On a server with two teams, a todo row has teamId A and projectId set to team B's project. Before this PR, chief or MCP create_todo did not check the project's team, so such rows can exist. A team-A MCP key calls run_builds with that todo id. requireTeamTodo passes, and startBuilds creates a build on team B's project. The claim payload then carries team B's repo with team A's GitHub credential (machines.ts githubExecCredential uses todoRow.teamId). The same call through chief now returns 404 and changes nothing. This is not a regression, since MCP run_builds never called requireProjectRow, but it leaves the two tool surfaces checking project ownership differently. The fix is the same as in chief: validate every task's project with requireProjectRow(db, row.projectId, ctx.teamId) before the loop, and do the same in schedule_todo.

suggestions.title: Open PR #1414 adds a hand split of project.githubRepo in ci-loop.ts that bypasses githubRepoOfProject; the Risk section names only a textual conflict with it

It checks `repoKind !== 'github' || githubRepo === null`, then `const slash = projRow.githubRepo.indexOf('/')` and `owner: projRow.githubRepo.slice(0, slash), repo: projRow.githubRepo.slice(slash + 1)`. The PR body says githubRepoOfProject is 'the one place the server splits a stored project.githubRepo', and asks #1467 and #1461 to route through it. For #1414 it mentions only a merge-tree conflict in ci-loop.ts ('keeps both changes').
suggestions.failurePath: Suppose #1414 merges after this PR and the conflict resolver keeps both changes as the body suggests. #1414's review-phase reconcile path (githubTarget) then builds `repos/owner/../pulls/...` requests for a stored `owner/..` row with the team token, which this PR set out to stop. Nothing in #1468 fails at this head. This is the docs/pr-review.md semantic-conflict check, so naming githubTarget in the Risk section (or in a comment on #1414) is the fix.

suggestions.title: Round 2 rewrote R7 so the CI poller's guard for an invalid stored githubRepo (ci-loop.ts) has no test at head
suggestions.evidence: The round-1 R7 (removed in ddb06ca4) put a todo straight into phase 'building' with a PR-bearing build and ran poller.sweep(). It asserted rec.calls == [], and mutations.txt M3 shows it was killed through that path. The new R7 calls completeStep first. At head, completeStep sends the todo to 'review' (builds.ts deliveredGithubPr now uses githubRepoOfProject). sweep() then selects candidates only where todo.phase = 'building' (ci-loop.ts:325), so pollOne and the guard at ci-loop.ts:212-223 never run. The `expect(rec.calls).toEqual([])` after the sweep (line 353) therefore passes whatever ci-loop.ts does. No other test sets up a building todo with an invalid stored repo: ci-loop.test.ts uses only 'octo/demo', null/local and hosted. The r2 mutation set (r2-mutations.txt) has no ci-loop.ts mutation.
suggestions.failurePath: Revert ci-loop.ts:212-224 to the origin/main form: `projRow.repoKind !== 'github' || projRow.githubRepo === null`, then slice at '/'. Every test at head still passes. In production, a todo that was already in 'building' with a PR before this change, in a project whose stored githubRepo is '../user' (the PR's Risk section says such tasks stay in building), would again make the poller send GET https://api.github.com/repos/../user/commits/<branch>/check-runs with the team token. fetch normalizes that to /user/commits/... This is exactly the ticket's 'stored value, no request' failure mode. The code at head is correct, but nothing would catch a regression of it. A test should set up the old R7 state directly: a todo inserted in 'building' with a prNumber build and an invalid stored repo, then sweep() and assert zero calls. That test could sit next to the new delivery-gate R7.

suggestions.title: Scope beyond the ticket: the todos team filter and whole-list refusal in run_builds and watch_todos
suggestions.failurePath: Ticket #1466 scopes the change to the dot-segment check and to adding teamId to the two requireProjectRow sites. The PR also does three things the ticket does not list. (1) Chief and MCP todos now always filter on the team (chief-tools.ts:268, mcp-face.ts:191). (2) run_builds now checks every task and its project before any startBuilds (chief-tools.ts:818-821), so a list with one bad id now starts nothing; before, the earlier tasks in the list were started. (3) watch_todos skips another team's task (chief-tools.ts:963-967). All three narrow cross-team reach or make the call all-or-nothing, and the PR body's Risk section names them, so the safety effect is positive. The run_builds change does alter same-team behavior, though: a list containing one missing id no longer starts the valid ids before it. That deserves the user's notice when merging.

suggestions.title: Clone URLs are still built from a stored invalid githubRepo
suggestions.failurePath: projectRepoRef (git.ts:129-132), toProjectRecord (git.ts:228-229) and the branch sync in routes-builds.ts:189-190 still use the raw stored value through githubCloneUrl. Take a row stored before this PR with githubRepo "../user". It yields https://github.com/../user.git, which URL parsing turns into github.com/user.git: a path with one segment that names no repository, so the clone fails. The host stays github.com, and none of the possible dot values ("../user", "./x", "owner/..", "owner/.", "../..") resolves to another real repository. So no token reaches a different host or repository. The PR's Risk section names this. Routing these through githubRepoOfProject in a follow-up would make the server's handling of stored rows consistent.
